sections.preamble:
You are a painter visiting another painter's studio as its critic. The studio is the folder you are in. You see the painting with the look tool and read the painter's journal and its note to you with the read tool. You don't paint.

You are not being evaluated in a quantifiable way.

toolsAdded.name: look
toolsAdded.description: Look at the canvas as it is now. Without options: the whole canvas, scaled down. crop: "x0,y0,x1,y1" in canvas units (two opposite corners), at full detail up to 1200 pixels a side; larger crops are scaled down. The reply gives the scale in pixels per canvas unit. mask: a global mask's name (or several, comma-separated), shown as outlines and a light fill over the view. mode: "value" (the picture in grays, its lightness alone, in the gallery light), "squint", "edges" (the picture's edges drawn over a dim gray of it: orange where an edge is hard, blue where it is soft, brighter the more the lightness changes across it; hard and soft as they read at the size of the image the look returns), "mirror", "relief" (a raking light on the paint's ridges and furrows), "gallery" (the light the picture hangs in) or several, comma-separated. light: "azimuth,elevation" in degrees for the relief light (default "135,25", from the upper left). size: the long side in pixels. grid: true, or a spacing in canvas units. survey: true surveys the whole canvas at full detail, as several tiles (with mode, not crop or size); a partial reply lists remaining tiles to read in separate turns. compare: the path of an earlier look, shown left of the current view; supply matching crop, mode and light options explicitly. ref: the path of a picture of the motif in this studio (a photograph, a study), fitted to the canvas's shape (scaled to cover it and centered, so a picture of another shape loses its edges) and shown left of the same view of the canvas: the same crop, size, mode and grid, as a picture pinned beside the easel. hold: the name of a knife (what is on it) or a pile (a fresh load), with at: "x,y" (canvas units): the loaded knife held up to the canvas there, its paint thick on the blade (crop sets the passage). Supports mode value, squint, relief or gallery and light; size, grid and mirror are unavailable with hold. It shows the paint on the knife, not how it would look laid. palette: true shows the palette board instead: each pile knifed out thick and smeared thin across a black stripe.

scratch.description: true: the scratch canvas beside the painting instead of the painting. It is set up as the painting's canvas was, with its own palette, brushes and variables, and its own log; nothing done there reaches the painting. It keeps its own clock: time spent or waited there doesn't pass for the painting.

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

content.text:
The painter has just ended a sitting at the easel, and you've come to see the painting.

Look at it as closely as you like: the whole canvas, detail crops, the value, squint, mirror, relief and gallery views and the palette. Read the painter's journal, notes/journal.md, and its note to you, notes/to_critic.md.

The painter's journal handoff lists the passages it has left open. Its latest list, quoted as the painter wrote it:

> Open passages: none

Then tell the painter what you would fix and why, as one painter talking to another: what you see, what it does to the picture and what you would do about it. Say which passage, if any, you would take up first, whether or not it is on the painter's list. Your last message is what the painter gets. It is saved in the studio as notes/critic.md, and the painter's next sitting opens with it. The painter decides what to do with it.

- day 1, 09:00: ## Sitting 1 — plan
  Concept 6: a ship's hull caught and half buried in a jagged pyramid of pack ice, cold blue Arctic sky.
  My own arrangement (not the Eismeer's): canvas 1050 mm, aspect 1.4 (W1000 x H714), linen 15/13, warm ground: knife layer white2/red earth1/ochre1 90µm, brushed top layer white8/ochre0.25/umber0.08 45µm (patchy, pinkish showing).
  Composition: horizon y=440. Pyramid apex ~(630,90), base ~250..950; low sun from the LEFT: left/upward faces lit warm, right flank in cool shadow, pyramid casts shadow right across the plain. Ship's bow (brig) thrust up-left out of the left shoulder at ~25°, bowsprit pointing into the empty left; mast stump leaning right across a lit slab. Dark lead of open water in left foreground narrowing to the pyramid base; large lit tilted slab bottom right; low distant bergs on horizon; a low mid-distance ridge at left.
  Studies on scratch (scratch-2, -3): lit ice vanished against a pale sky -> sky top must be deeper (~value 130-150) for the apex to read; the hull read as a fin until bowsprit + mast were added; the hull looked flying because no ice under/in front of it -> add slabs under the bow and one slab tip crossing in front of the hull side, extend the base left to ~250.
- day 3, 16:19: ## Lay-in (day 1–3)
  - Pencil HB underdrawing, all slab polygons, hull, horizon (ruled), water lead. Saved globals: back, front (faces {pts, kind, name}), hull, bowsprit, mast, waterlead, farL, farR, midridge, castshadow, horizon=440. Masks iceAll, hullM, skyM, waterM, plainM.
  - Thin lay-in, turps 0.5: shadow faces uS (white1/cobalt1/smalt0.6/umber0.3), mid uM, hull uH (umber2/black0.5/red earth0.3), water uW (Prussian1/black1/umber0.3). Lit faces left as ground. Turps 0.5 lay-in of umber/black dried tacky->dry in ~1 day.
  - Sky: body paint, no thinner, 5 piles graded by y (k1 white1.2/cobalt1.2/Prussian0.08 at top ... k4 white8/Naples0.35/cobalt0.15 at horizon, k5 warm white8/Naples0.5/rose0.08 low left), work hand body coverage 2 fill, clip, then ONE blend pass angle 0. Result: smooth graded sky, top value ~165, horizon ~215. Good: keep. Single blend is enough; soft cloud-like mottling remains (pleasant).
  - Ice faces day 3 over dry lay-in: body paint graded per face top->bottom with two piles; lit iL1 (white6/Naples0.14) = value 232, warm. Mid iM1/iM2 came out ~210 = too light; shadow flank C came out ~190, too light. => restate shadows darker once dry.
  - Scratch trial (scratch-8): body shadow mixes on fresh ground: white1.2/cobalt0.9/smalt0.6/umber0.15 -> 161; with green earth+Prussian -> 154 (greener); white0.6/cobalt1/Prussian0.15/umber0.4 -> 115; white1.6/... Naples/rose -> 172 (warm grey-blue); white0.8/cobalt0.9/smalt0.5/rose0.15 -> violet ~(too violet). Glazes medium 0.75-0.8 over light dry body: cobalt+rose -> lavender veil, Prussian/cobalt -> turquoise; glazes shift hue more than value: use body repaint for value, glaze for hue/translucency.
- day 12, 11:14: ## Day 9–12: body layer of masses
  - Shadow flank C restated with sC1 (white1/cobalt0.9/smalt0.6/umber0.2) -> sC2 (warmer, Naples+rose) graded by y, + sG (green earth/Prussian) blotches by stretched noise. Value ~165-175. Ae crevice sDeep/sDeepG ~115-130.
  - MISTAKE: paintFace over the whole polygon C painted over B/H parts that were in front -> had to wipe (rag dipped 0.8, pressure 0.7, 2 passes; wet over dry body -> lifted fully). Then built occlusion helpers: order (back..front), infront(name), visible(name), restate(name, piles). ALWAYS paint visible(name), not poly(face).
  - Hull body: hL2 (umber2/black0.6/white0.35/red0.2/ochre0.2) at bow -> hD2 (umber2/black1.4/red0.15/Prussian0.05) aft, filbert 4 angle 0.45. Value ~70-80 bow, ~60 aft. Hull's tail end that poked past B was wiped (rag width 14-16 dipped 0.9 several passes over wet hull on dry B) and B restated with litW; new slab R (432..492, 322..445) now crosses the hull in front so it is 'swallowed' by ice. Mast break notched with sky pile sf1 (white3.4/cobalt1/Prussian0.032 = sky value ~200 at y 210).
  - Plain: pl1 (white6/cobalt0.9/rose0.1/Naples0.15/umber0.08) at horizon ~212 -> pl3 (white6/cobalt0.55/Naples0.45/umber0.08) ~220 in front. (Trial: white6/cobalt0.45... only came 222-226; needed double the cobalt to get below 215.) Foreground shadow band under 'fshadow' outline (broken char): fs1/fs2 lavender-grey ~188.
  - Assessment after masses: high-key, cold; darks only hull + water. Pyramid reads as paper cut-outs: needs slab thickness edges, snow lips, broken edges, contact shadows, rubble at base, cast shadows to the right. Water lead too saturated navy -> repaint dark slate-green with reflections. Big lit slab bottom right is flat -> model it. Consider deepening bottom-left corner as repoussoir, a deeper accent in the Ae crevice, and a cobalt glaze at the zenith.
- day 16, 12:11: ## Day 16: water, far bergs, sky glaze; articulation trials
  - Water lead repainted body: wD (black1/Prussian0.35/umber0.4/white0.7/green earth0.3) left -> wM (black0.6/Prussian0.25/umber0.2/white2/cobalt0.4) toward the narrow end. Slate green-grey, ~70-110. Good, less navy.
  - Far bergs: bL/bS small detail-hand polygons on horizon. Fine, low contrast.
  - Sky zenith glaze: gz2 (cobalt1/Prussian0.04/umber0.06, medium 0.8) graded with 'clear' (white0.3/cobalt0.05 medium 0.95) over top 260 units, then 3 blends (angles 0.2,-0.2,0). Over dry sky body: top deepened ~165 -> ~150, deeper cobalt. Trial (scratch-12) showed a single glaze leaves a feathered vertical seam where the passes meet; 2-3 blends cure it. Result on painting: good, faint diagonal blend tracks visible only in a close crop.
  - Trials (scratch-13/14) for cast shadows on dry lit white: glaze cobalt/smalt/rose med 0.7 -> 209 (light veil), med 0.55 -> 200, med 0.4 -> lavender ~180 but glazes leave small holes; body csC (white2/cobalt0.65/smalt0.4/Naples0.15/rose0.06/umber0.05) -> 189 opaque, controllable: USE BODY for cast shadows.
  - Thinner 0.5 body over dry white -> nearly invisible. Scumble hand with thinner 0.3 -> blotchy dabs: avoid.
  - Body paint with edge="lost" over dry paint still makes a visible seam (hard-ish) -> for gradients over dry paint, repaint the whole face with graded piles instead.
  - Rigger strata lines (strata pile white1.6/cobalt0.9/smalt0.5/green earth0.2/umber0.1, load 0.4, pressure 0.25->0.15) along a dark thickness edge read beautifully as layered ice -> vary spacing, break some. Rigger cracks via gesture+wobble became snaky S-curves -> use straight polyline strokes for cracks. A filbert 3 snow-lip stroke (white6/Naples0.12) along a sunlit top edge of a shadow face reads as a rim of light: good.
- day 16, 13:48: ## Critic visit 1 (day 16) — summary and my decisions
  Critic: upper half holds (sky, central blade, hull vs sky). Lower half unresolved:
  1. Ice doesn't sit on the ground: no edge where lit faces meet the plain; blue bands under the front slab (De) and pillar (He) read as undersides of floating boxes (we look down on them!); pyramid's cast shadow missing. -> Repaint plain around base; lay the pyramid's cast shadow as one big body-paint shape (~180-185 vs plain 215-220) running right and back to the horizon, continuous with the shadowed fronts of slabs E and F; turn De/He into snow; broken contact darks at every base.
  2. Water lead = flat bar, ends in empty snow -> re-route: wide at left edge, rising steeply, slipping behind the front slab ending ~ (460-480, 535).
  3. Hull rests on the slab Q along a tangent -> break Q's top up over the hull's lower third with jagged rubble; a slab tip crossing the hull at x 360-400; a lit rail/snow line along the gunwale; keep ship detail very fine.
  4. Lit ice merges into one cream shape -> cast shadows between blocks (mid-values 150-175) BEFORE chips/lips: R on B, C on G; deeper accent in Ae crevice.
  Smaller: Be sliver reads as glassy ghost -> commit as a shadowed edge (~170); foreground band deepen a step + warmer toward bottom-left; FG slab: decided shadowed, give its top edge breakage later; keep left plain empty.
  I agree with all of it. Order: dry -> plain/base -> cast shadow -> lead -> inter-block shadows -> bury hull -> contact darks -> then detail.
  Trial (scratch-15): covering dry dark water (wD) with plain pile pl2: one broad pass cov 1.6 leaves a few dark streaks; broad 2.5 + body 1.5 covers cleanly.
- day 31, 16:39: ## Day 24–31: seating the cluster (after critic 1)
  - De/He removed from occlusion order (front2); repainted as plain/snow along with old water path (broad cov 2.5 + body 1.5: covers dry dark water cleanly).
  - New lead: outline 'leadO' (broken char) wide at left (604..700) rising to a tip at (482,514) behind front slab D1. Painted wD->wM body cov 2.2, angle -0.17. Mask leadM (global).
  - Pyramid cast shadow: outline castO (soft) from base (612..1000, y 430..560) to right edge; body cs0 (white1.1/cobalt0.7/smalt0.5/Naples0.08/rose0.08/umber0.12) -> cs1; value ~166 near base vs plain 218. First pass with cs1/cs2 only reached 185 -> too light, second pass with cs0 needed. Shadow's near edge wiped below castEdge outline with a narrow dipped rag (width 12) to make it broken/crisp. E restated in shadow (cs1/cs0/sG).
  - Inter-block shadows: B restated cooler/greyer (litCool/mB), Be committed as warm lit edge (litWarm) instead of glassy sky-value sliver; B's shadow on A (shBA poly), R's shadow on B (shRB), hull's shadow on Q (hullShadowQ), wedge of shadow between D1 and H (cs0).
  - Contact darks: round 3.2 point 0.6, ctD (white0.9/cobalt0.9/smalt0.5/rose0.06/umber0.25) load 0.6 pressure 0.5-0.7 along slab bottoms: reads as a crisp blue line. OK but a bit 'drawn': later break it with rubble.
  - Hull buried: two new shards S1 (346..409, 315..400) and S2 (412..446, 365..397) cross the hull's lower side; added to order (globals newSlabs).
  - Foreground band repainted deeper/warmer: fs1 top -> fg1 (white1.6/cobalt0.6/smalt0.4/umber0.22/Naples0.12/rose0.04 ~178) -> fg2 (more umber, red earth ~167) toward bottom-left. Bottom-left now ~150, centre ~178, right ~183.
  - Hull planking: 10 plank seams (round 1.3 point 1, plankD black1.5/umber1 medium 0.15, load 0.5-0.7) along interpolated lines between gunwale and keel; light lower lips (plankL) on the bow half; wale = round 3 dark band. Mast/bowsprit restated woodD core + woodL lit edge (round 2), rail shadow, broken snow runs along the rail cap (snowW round 2.2 load 0.55), lit stem, rigger stays/shrouds/hanging rope (woodD load 0.4 pressure ~0.2) -> fine and convincing at full size.
- day 31, 19:27: ## Day 31 evening: rubble at the base
  - Block helper (global blockShapes/paintBlock(x,y,w,h,seed,inShadow,avoid)): front face (mB/mA half-light), top (litWarm), right face (sC1), cast shadow to the right (cs0); in-shadow version cs0/shTop/shDeep. Trial scratch-17/18: first versions (upright box + L-shaped shadow) read as cubes/bricks; leaning top edge with 2 jag points + depth offset (0.8,-0.3)*dep reads as ice blocks. Hand 'detail', filbert width w*0.12 (1.2..4), coverage 3, fill.
  - slabPiece(faces, seed, avoid) for hand-drawn pieces (list front-most first). Big plate in front of Q (330..406, 481..511) + its shadow: reads very well. Upright shard at the lead tip; fallen slab between D1/H.
  - Base rubble lit side (13 blocks, x 238..603), shadow side (12 blocks x 668..962 at y~555) + one lit block at 985.
  - MISTAKE: 'tongues' of shadow laid in front of the shadowed rubble read as detached rectangles floating on the snow. Lifted them: rag width 8, dip 1.0, pressure 0.95, 4 x 2 passes rotating angle -> clean (paint was minutes old, over dry plain).
  - Lifted 4 lonely scattered blocks in the left plain the same way (tiny ghosts remain = read as distant chips, fine).
  - rubbleM global = union of all rubble masks (protect in later passes).
- day 35, 21:42: ## Day 35: smoothing the big faces, water
  - Big faces C, Q, E, D2 and the foreground band repainted with hand 'broad' (filbert 8-12) + one blend along the fall line, over dry body. Trial scratch-20: body hand (filbert 6) leaves blotchy dabs ("leopard spots"); broad + one blend gives a smooth graded face with a few long streaks = ice. Use broad+blend for large faces from now on.
  - Water lead: repainted broad + blend (waterBody = leadM minus the bank wall ribbon). Far-bank wall = short round strokes of edgeG (white2/cobalt0.6/green earth0.45/Prussian0.05/smalt0.2) following bankTop, width 5.5 -> 2 with distance, then one blend along it. Reflection strokes reflW under the wall, and ripple lines; ripple lines were too bright/graphic -> blended once (angle -0.24) -> soft streaks remain: good.
  - Far right: lit far plain above a jagged shadow edge (farEdge) at x>944; shadow gap between C/E/G filled with cs0.
  - Remaining look: the forms are clean geometric facets = poster-like. Next campaign: detail (broken silhouettes as small ice teeth pushed out in the ice's own colour, not sky patches; fractures; strata on lit faces; snow ledges; translucent turquoise at thin edges; the arch outline on top of H to be repainted; a few scattered blocks in the right lit plain; foreground detail along the near bank; maybe a spar lying in the snow).
- day 45, 23:46: ## Critic visit 2 (day 45) — summary
  Poster look comes from 3 habits: (1) every plane gets one of two values (cream lit / lavender shadow); D1's right face (D2) lit-looking although right-facing planes should be in shadow; (2) every edge equally hard; (3) same motif repeated at one scale (bead row of rubble at y~550 = brick curb; dice with drop shadows; far-bank wall beads; embossed zigzag fractures = piped icing).
  Do, in order: (a) base x450-1000: D2 into shadow/half-tone ~190; paint out bead row and dice; rebuild foot as TALUS: plates (wider than tall, half sunk, seen from above), few big + many small in 2-3 clumps, snow drifts between, silhouette rising/falling; one or two deepest accents (crevD/sDeep + umber) under overhangs; repaint grey 'pipe' on H top. (b) lit-face ORDER: left-facing lightest, faces toward us a step down, tops bright warm but soft; turn value toward rolling edges. (c) warm bounce in shadow feet (C, E, right pillar lower third, Naples/rose); greener thin edges/undercuts; (d) remove embossed fractures: cracks = steps between planes, one or two on C only; remove blue ticks on S1/S2. (e) edges: hard at apex/blade/hull/nearest tops/lead far bank; lost lit-lit and shadow-shadow; soft snow and receding shadow edges. (f) detail where hull meets ice (ice over gunwale, sprung planks, darkest dark under hull), thickness edges strata (D1 top, FG slab, talus plates, far-bank wall), near foreground (tilted plates on near bank, loose floes near narrow end, FG lit lip with breakage). Keep detail out of big lit faces, C, sky, left plain.
  Smaller: foreground shadow band top edge reads as hills -> flatten into long near-horizontal runs or give a lit crest; far-left mid-ridge ruled base -> sink behind snow line; pane between C and right pillar (Ge/J ~810-850, 260-335) reads as glass -> commit; farEdge staircase -> vary; spars too heavy (X / windmill) -> thin/lighten outer thirds, broken tip.
- day 49, 05:20: ## Day 48–49: lit-face order, talus
  - Lit-face order applied with restateBroad(m, piles, angle, tool, seed) = broad hand cov 2 + one blend (global helper). A lightest (litWarm top -> litW, litCool rolling toward its right edge, nearEdge() weight); B litW->litCool, mB at its rolling edge; G litWarm->litCool; D1 (faces us) a step down: litCool->mB; H likewise; D2 put into shadow cs1 + warm bounce (bounceW = white2.2/cobalt0.55/smalt0.35/Naples0.3/rose0.07/umber0.04) at its foot. Smoothed R, S1, S2 (removing ticks/fractures). C and E restated with bounceW in lower third (warmer feet), J committed as shadow (cs1/sC2). Lit cap strokes (filbert 3 litWarm) along D1 and H tops.
  - Fractures removed by these restatements (zigzags gone from D1, H, E, C, G, B).
  - Dice/bead rubble painted out (mask rebuilt from blockShapes seeds; covered with pl2/pl3 in light, cs0/cs1 in the shadow zone, body cov 2.5).
  - Talus: new plateShapes/paintPlate(cx,cy,w,d,th,rot,tiltUp,seed,mode,avoid): plates seen from above (top quad + thin front + right edge + cast shadow in light). Modes lit/edge/shade. Clumps L1 (245..320,492..510), L2, L3 (498..552), under H, S1 (666..728), S2 (800..884), S3 (940..985). talusM global.
  - MISTAKE: auto mode chose 'lit' for many plates in the shadow zone (castM's soft outline doesn't cover y 530-560 well) -> big cream houses in the shadow. Wiped (rag w8-10 dip 1.0, 8 single passes — a rag fills fast over fresh thick detail paint: 'whole cloth full' warnings, take fresh rag each pass) and repainted with explicit 'shade'/'edge'. Drifts from soft outlines looked like snowmen heads -> wiped. Residual ghost (house plate) covered with broad cs1 + blends over a ramp mask.
  - Result: D1 now a solid; the base has an irregular talus; shadow talus plates with lit tops read well.
- day 49, 07:15: ## Day 49: hull junction, spars, foreground band
  - Hull junction: crushed pocket under the bow keel (crevD + woodD, deepest dark in the ice); small lit chips + a leaning shard (slabPiece) in the pocket; sprung planks (round 1.6 woodD/woodL short curved strokes) near S1's tip and at 392,345; ice ridge BEHIND the hull above the gunwale (behindRidge poly, lit litWarm with sC1 right-facing facets) so the hull reads sunk among slabs, shrouds restated over it.
  - MISTAKE: a lit slab 'riding over the gunwale' read as a bench/table -> wiped (rag w8 dip 1.0, 5 passes) leaving a slight light trace on the rail (reads as snow; kept).
  - Spars thinned: sky-coloured band over the outer half of bowsprit/mast underside + broken tip notch. First sky pile skyM2 (white4.2/cobalt1/Prussian0.03/Naples0.1) too light (~206 vs sky 189-199 there) -> visible halo -> wiped (rag w6 dip 1.0 x4) and redone with graded skyT1 (white3.4/cobalt1/Pr0.032 = 198) -> skyT3 (white4.6/cobalt1/Pr0.03/Naples0.12 = 206) by y. Matches; spars now thinner, broken tips.
  - Foreground shadow edge re-drawn as a flat stepped perspective edge (shEdge: long near-horizontal runs with small steps), lit plain above restated pl2/pl3; whole band below repainted fs1->fg1->fg2 broad cov 2.5 + blend (first try cut off at y=640 left a seam -> repainted the whole band to the bottom in one pass).
  - LESSON: a failed chunk restores Lua variables too: piles created in a failed chunk don't exist; and a palette scrape inside a failed chunk didn't happen. After a failure, re-check palette() before reusing names.
- day 54, 09:31: ## Day 54: foreground and finishing touches of sitting 1
  - Near bank of the lead: three plate pieces (piece() helper with modes stop/sfront/refl/green etc.) + an upright lit shard at 196..228,600..648 with a green reflection. nearM global.
  - Far-bank wall repainted as a continuous band (wallM; mA/edgeG/sC1 + blend) with a broken lit lip (round 1.3 litWarm), a broken dark waterline (rigger crevD) and faint strata -> the bead chain is gone.
  - Floating brash (floe helper: top + edgeG side + reflection, clipped to leadM) along the narrow end and the middle of the lead. floatM global.
  - Left mid-ridge sunk behind a low lit snow swell (swellCrest) with a broken crest line.
  - farEdge2 (far right): varied hummocks with lit left tips.
  - FG slab top edge broken with teeth (slabTop up, pl2 down). MISTAKE before: a lit lip + lit thickness edge along FG made it read as a cream ramp/sidewalk -> wiped clean (rag w8 x6).
  - Ae thickness edge: turquoise glaze (Prussian0.25/cobalt0.6/green earth0.6, medium 0.75) graded with clr (medium 0.95) at the top 230 units + blend: very subtle greening (scratch-25: same on dry sDeep - subtle). OK.

  ## HANDOFF (end of sitting 1, painting day 54)
  State: all masses laid and seated; a talus at the base; hull buried with crushed pocket; spars thinned; lead with far-bank wall, floes; foreground band flattened. Paint near the base (talus, right plates), near bank pieces, floes, FG teeth and Ae glaze are fresh (open/setting) — wait ~5-6 days before working over them.
  Open passages:
  - Right base talus (x 660-1000, y 540-570): the older small shadow blocks from baseSh still sit in a row between the new plates; break the row further (paint some out into cs0 snow, vary sizes), one deeper accent under the big plate at ~826,550.
  - Edges across the cluster: still uniformly hard (edges view). Lose lit-against-lit (D1/H, B/A lower) and shadow-against-shadow (C/E/G/F joins); soften receding cast-shadow edges; keep hard: apex/blade vs sky, hull vs ice, nearest slab tops, lead far bank.
  - Left shoulder (x 240-470, y 330-500, slabs Q/T/R/S1 and the lit facets LQ1/LQ2): many crisp cream facets of similar value; rank values (faces toward us a step down) and add a deeper accent under the plate below Q.
  - Hull: fine planks are good; consider a lit rail line all along the sunward gunwale, a little snow on the deck edge, and greying the planks' light lips that look a touch regular.
  - Lit plain right of the pyramid (x 480-1000, y 560-630): empty; leave mostly quiet; perhaps a few half-sunk plates + their shadows at varied scale (plates, not cubes).
  - Foreground band (y 590-714): flat; consider soft snow undulation (sastrugi) and one or two near plates on the right near the FG slab foot.
  - Sky: done; optional faint high thin cloud streaks near horizon? (probably leave).
  - Signature: not yet (bottom left, small, in the shadow band).

  Lessons to carry (hypotheses unless noted):
  - Large faces: hand 'broad' + one blend along the fall line gives smooth ice; body hand leaves blotchy dabs.
  - Small forms: plates seen from above (top quad + thin front + right edge + shadow) read as ice; upright boxes with drop shadows read as dice/bricks.
  - Explicitly choose lit/shade mode per piece; the castM mask's soft outline misreports the shadow zone near y 530-560.
  - Wiping fresh detail paint: rag width 6-10, dip 1.0, pressure 0.95, many single passes with a fresh rag each — a single rag fills fast ('whole cloth full').
  - Sky-coloured patches must match the local sky value (sky is ~198 at y 210, ~206 at y 270 near the hull): use graded skyT1/skyT3 by y.

content.text:
I'd call it finished. I looked at the whole canvas in normal colour, value, squint, mirror, gallery, edges and relief, and up close at the hull, the base, the lead and the near plane. Nothing in it is still a fault worth another sitting.

**What holds.** At gallery distance the picture comes down to four things: the lit blade against the deepest sky, the dark hull with its two spars, the lead running up into the base, and the shadow band carrying everything down to the frame. In the value view only three things are dark: the hull, the water and the green foreground slab. They make a loose triangle across the canvas, and the blade's light sits inside it. The empty left plain melts into a warm low sky that's almost the same value, so the bowsprit points into open air. That emptiness is doing work; don't fill it. Your last two campaigns took things out (dice, bead rows, trays, piped cracks) and put whole planes in their place, and the canvas looks like it.

**Small things I still see.** None of these would make me pick up a brush.

1. **The floes in the lead.** From about 345,580 up to 470,528 the floes still read faintly as a row of evenly spaced white discs, like runway lights leading to the base. They're the one place where the eye reads a pattern rather than ice.
2. **The snow bank at E's foot** (about 690–830, 510–555). It's the only rounded silhouette in a picture built from straight breaks, so it reads a little like a whale's back. In the gallery view it settles down as a drift.
3. **The near plate in the band.** Its far right corner, where it meets the frame, is slightly rounded. In the value view it's a gentle shift inside the shadow, which is what you wanted.

The mast-foot wrap and the faint diagonal blend tracks in the sky only show in close crops.

**Why I'd leave them.** Your notes have proved this three times: on this canvas a local patch over dry paint leaves a ghost, a rod or a tube. Each item above would be that kind of patch, and each sits in a passage that works at viewing distance. Fixing them risks more than it gains.

**If you still have to take one up.** Do the floes, and only the floes. It's the smallest, safest job: a dark field, a pile you've already matched (wM4), and you've dropped coins cleanly before. Take out one or two in the middle of the run so the trail breaks into a cluster and a gap, and stop there. I'd still rather you didn't.

**On edges.** Your conclusion is the right one: decide which edges are lost in the wet first body layer, not at the end. The even crispness now reads as this picture's manner, and it's consistent from apex to frame. That consistency is worth more than a softened stretch that looks patched.

*The Ice Keeps Her* is done. Sign-off agreed.
